source_snapshot.purpose_facts: Build netperf 2.7.0, start netserver, run an engineer-selected TCP or UDP test from a client, and compare the result with the NIC specification.
procedure_facts: Build and install netperf 2.7.0 from the HewlettPackard GitHub archive.
Run `netperf -t type_of_testing -H SERVER_IP -l test_time -P port` for TCP or a similar UDP command.
source_conflicts: The generic command uses `-P port`, but Netperf 2.7.x documents control and data socket ports with different options and `-P` is not a generic control-port placeholder.
missing_source_information: Server/client placement, NIC path and IPs.
TCP/UDP test name, direction, duration, control/data ports, message/request sizes and stream count.
Numeric NIC-spec threshold and repeat/aggregation rule.

original_test_intent.statement: Build the approved Netperf 2.7.0 tool and run a specifically approved TCP or UDP performance profile between a designated client and netserver for the intended 120-minute machine window, then compare the complete result with the matching NIC specification.
must_preserve: Netperf/netserver client-server measurement on the target NIC path.
Engineer selection of TCP or UDP test semantics before execution.
NIC-spec comparison and host/network health evidence.
120-minute machine-time intent unless the engineer defines it as an envelope rather than workload duration.
must_not_infer: TCP_STREAM as a substitute for an unspecified test type.
That `-P` names the netserver control port.
Server/client roles, data direction, ports or thresholds from neighboring cases.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 correctly requires an approved source/toolchain, peer, endpoint roles, path, protocol/profile, duration/port, isolation, full build output and specification.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: V2 repeats the source's `-P <PORT>` example without identifying its option-semantics error and does not force reconciliation of the unspecified `test_time` with Machine Time 120; these can silently produce the wrong measurement.

related_records: The preceding iperf case cannot supply this Netperf test type, port semantics or duration.
applicable_history.precedence_application: Generic placeholders require an engineer decision; they cannot be resolved by selecting TCP_STREAM or 60 seconds for convenience.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Automation is feasible only after the engineer freezes the exact Netperf test and option syntax, endpoint roles, duration, NIC profile and threshold. Do not run the generic source or DeepSeek command.

conditions_present: Netperf 2.7.0 source location and client/server architecture are identified.
missing: Exact test/profile, roles/path, 120-minute interpretation, correct ports/options, source commit/hash, threshold and approvals.
provider: Lab owner supplies isolated peer and endpoint access.
Software owner approves source, build and install scope.
safe_read_only_work: Inventory NIC/BDF/driver/firmware/link/MTU/offloads/NUMA/routes and current counters on both hosts.
Inspect existing Netperf versions and validate proposed options with help output without starting netserver or traffic.
prohibited_until_resolved: Source build/install, listener, traffic, network changes, log clearing or PASS.
closure_evidence: Signed profile states test name, direction, sizes, duration/repeats and correct control/data ports.
Approved source hash/build target and two-endpoint map are available.
Comparable numeric threshold and health limits are signed.

revision_candidate.test_name: Run an Approved Netperf 2.7.0 NIC Performance Profile
revision_candidate.purpose: Measure the exact engineer-approved TCP or UDP Netperf profile between a designated client and netserver on one NIC path, preserving the approved duration and workload semantics, and compare complete performance and health evidence with the matching NIC specification.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Two approved hosts on an isolated Ethernet path, with the exact NIC ports/BDFs, driver/firmware, negotiated link, NUMA placement and Netperf 2.7.0 build identified. TCP_STREAM, TCP_RR, UDP_STREAM and UDP_RR are distinct tests.
revision_candidate.target_scope: One signed client/server pair, NIC path and Netperf test. Machine Time is 120 minutes; the engineer must state whether this is one run, repeated runs or the test envelope. No 60-second substitution is allowed.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Checksummed Netperf 2.7.0 source/commit and build policy; client/server placement and addresses; NIC/link/IP/VLAN/MTU/offload/NUMA profile; exact test name/direction, socket/message/request sizes, duration/repeats, confidence/aggregation, control and data ports using documented option placement; peer capacity; numeric metric/units/threshold; traffic and listener approval; recovery.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Preserve baseline mapping/counters/logs, build the pinned source with visible configure/make output in an approved path, and verify binary versions/help. Start netserver only on the signed server and record PID/listen address/control port. From the client run the frozen Netperf command using the correct global and post-`--` test options; never use the source's generic `-P port` blindly. Capture every repeat and full output, monitor both endpoints, stop only the recorded daemon, restore changes and verify connectivity.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Isolated path and peer; exact test/profile/duration/ports approved; package/license/install location approved; listener exposure constrained; baseline health acceptable; abort limits and restoration ready.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Source commit/archive hash; configure/make/install logs; binary versions/help; endpoint/NIC/BDF/driver/firmware/link/MTU/offload/NUMA map; exact commands with option placement; server PID/listener; complete per-run output and confidence/aggregation; throughput or transaction-rate and latency where applicable; both-end counters/CPU/logs; duration proof; daemon shutdown, restoration and final health.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Signed NIC specification for the exact Netperf test, direction, link/profile, message/request sizes, duration and aggregation. Pass requires complete comparable runs meeting numeric thresholds with no disallowed drops/errors/instability; a different Netperf test or option interpretation is invalid.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Do not use password injection or disable host-key checks; suppress build errors; install unpinned source globally; expose netserver; guess test type, roles, ports or duration; saturate production links; clear evidence logs; kill unrelated processes; or claim PASS from truncated output.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Network owner signs test/profile/spec and traffic window; endpoint owners approve peer/listener/path; software owner approves build/install; a human authorizes traffic and judges PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Humans resolve the generic profile and port/duration semantics. An Agent may build and run only the frozen command, monitor and collect evidence after gates; it may not choose TCP_STREAM/UDP or reinterpret Machine Time.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Stop client and recorded netserver, preserve outputs/counters/logs, remove or retain installed artifacts per policy, restore network/firewall settings and confirm both hosts and the path are healthy before rerun.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Test type/roles/path/duration/options/spec/approval is unresolved; source/build verification fails; listener binds unexpectedly; production impact, error storm, peer bottleneck, host instability, monitoring loss or failed restoration occurs.

identified_defects: Generic test type leaves throughput versus request/response semantics undefined.
`-P port` is not a safe generic Netperf control-port placeholder.
DeepSeek substitutes TCP_STREAM and 60 seconds despite Machine Time 120.
reason_for_change: Prevent execution of a syntactically plausible but semantically wrong Netperf profile and require an explicit decision on the 120-minute intent.

new_technical_evidence.title: Care and Feeding of Netperf 2.7.X
new_technical_evidence.supports: Netperf uses distinct client/server executables and distinct TCP/UDP stream and request-response tests; global and test-specific options have different meanings.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The intended test, duration and port layout are not defined by the testcase.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-Performance Networking-00033-V004
new_technical_evidence.supports: Netperf 2.7.0 build, generic TCP/UDP commands, NIC-spec criterion and 30/120-minute metadata.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Profile, roles, duration and threshold remain open.

removed_ambiguities: Rejects the erroneous generic port placeholder.
Separates package/profile prerequisites from permanent blocking.
resolved_blockers: Source, peer and profile can be supplied; none alone makes the case permanently non-automatable.
remaining_blockers: Engineer must choose exact profile, option syntax, duration/aggregation and NIC acceptance rule.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 catches a command-option defect and prevents silent substitution of TCP_STREAM/60 seconds, while retaining V2's sound build, isolation and evidence controls.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The material defects are explicit and this case was not selected for isolated contract validation.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 resolves dependencies but repeats an unsafe generic port form and permits profile/duration choice without elevating the engineer decision.
